slides.title: Raise prices in 2027 where we have pricing power — and fix SMB before we reprice it

paragraphs.text: PALISADE DOCS  ·  2027 PRICING PLAN
Raise prices in 2027 where we have pricing power — and fix SMB before we reprice it
Should Palisade raise prices while customer churn is rising, and if so, how?
For: Ravi Menon (CEO) and the leadership team  ·  Decision meeting, December 2026
Prepared November 2026 from the internal briefing pack only (synthetic benchmark data; no external research)

slides.title: Yes, raise prices in 2027 — but by segment: mid-market and enterprise from January, SMB only after a test

paragraphs.text: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
Yes, raise prices in 2027 — but by segment: mid-market and enterprise from January, SMB only after a test
Churn is rising in one place

SMB monthly logo churn rose 2.0% → 3.1%; mid-market 0.6% → 0.8%; enterprise flat at 0.2%. Within SMB, the 2025 50%-off promotion cohort explains ~90% of the increase. Other SMB customers: 2.0% → 2.1%.
Price matters — but not where the CFO plan applies it hardest
Core SMB churners cite price no more than in 2025 (18% vs 19%). But promo churners do (52%) after their discount ended, and Inkwell’s $9 Starter has cut our contested SMB win rate from 51% to 38%.
$10.3M is a headline, not a 2027 number
12% × all ARR ignores renewal timing and enterprise caps: only $7.6M is capturable in 2027, and an SMB churn response cuts that to ~$5.0–6.3M, losing ~320–640 SMB customers.
Recommendation

Mid-market +10% at renewal ($3.5M) · Enterprise to contract terms — 7% where capped, 10% otherwise ($0.8M) · Hold SMB list prices in H1, run a controlled renewal test and an activation programme. = $4.3M, up to ~$5.1M if the April/July checkpoints pass.
What it delivers
If segments repeat trailing NRR, ARR reaches ~$98.3M (+14.2%); the 15% goal ($98.9M) needs ≥$0.7M new-logo ARR or the checkpoint upside. NRR stays ~114%, far above the 100% floor.
Source: Palisade Docs briefing pack, Nov 2026 (synthetic benchmark data). All ARR effects are end-2027 run-rate; see appendix for method.

slides.notes: The one-page answer. Everything after this slide is the support.

slides.title: The plan must add $12.9M of ARR with NRR above 100% — and only $65M of today’s $86M can be repriced in 2027

paragraphs.text: DECISION CRITERIA
The plan must add $12.9M of ARR with NRR above 100% — and only $65M of today’s $86M can be repriced in 2027
ARR by segment and whether it renews in 2027, $M
2027 ARR goal: +15% (+$12.9M) on today’s $86.0M
Net revenue retention guardrail; today ~109% ARR-weighted (SMB 94%, mid-market 112%, enterprise 118%)
ARR that renews — and so can be repriced — in 2027 (76% of total)
Enterprise: 60% of ARR is under contracts that cap annual increases at 7%.
Renewal share: SMB 100% · mid-market 85% · enterprise 40%. Customers: SMB 5,900 · mid-market 1,350 · enterprise 150.
Source: Palisade Docs briefing pack, Nov 2026 (synthetic benchmark data) — sections 3, 5 and 8.

slides.notes: Price changes apply at renewal. All SMB ARR renews in 2027, 85% of mid-market, 40% of enterprise. 60% of enterprise ARR is capped at 7% a year; we assume the cap is spread evenly across renewing and non-renewing enterprise contracts.

slides.title: Churn rose in SMB; mid-market edged up and enterprise is flat

paragraphs.text: WHERE CHURN IS RISING
Churn rose in SMB; mid-market edged up and enterprise is flat
Monthly logo churn by segment, %
The rise is an SMB story
SMB is 80% of customers but 24% of ARR ($21.0M).
Mid-market and enterprise ($65M, 76% of ARR) still grow from their base: NRR 112% and 118%.
SMB NRR is 94% — the only segment below 100%.
Do not use the board’s “1.4% → 2.3%”
It is undefined and does not match Table 1 on either weighting (customer-weighted 1.7% → 2.6%; ARR-weighted 0.8% → 1.2%). Action: report churn by segment and cohort.
Source: Palisade Docs briefing pack, Nov 2026 (synthetic benchmark data) — Table 1 (monthly logo churn, H1 2025 vs H1 2026).

slides.notes: The board dashboard figure 1.4% → 2.3% is not defined and cannot be reproduced from Table 1: customer-weighted churn is 1.7% → 2.6% and ARR-weighted 0.8% → 1.2% (using mid-2026 counts). We use segment figures throughout and recommend finance define the board metric.

slides.title: Inside SMB, the 2025 promotion cohort explains ~90% of the churn increase

paragraphs.text: WHY SMB CHURN ROSE
Inside SMB, the 2025 promotion cohort explains ~90% of the churn increase
SMB monthly logo churn, %
Promo cohort’s share of SMB customers (2,100 of 5,900) vs. its share of SMB customers leaving each month (~103 of ~183)
Share sending ≥5 documents in month one: promo cohort vs. other cohorts. Low-activation customers churn ~3× as often.
The worst is probably behind us
Discounts ended Aug 2025–Feb 2026 and most promo leavers left within two months. The cohort is only $4.4M of ARR — 5% of the total.

Source: Palisade Docs briefing pack, Nov 2026 (synthetic benchmark data) — section 6. Promo-cohort churn is implied: (5,900 × 3.1% − 3,800 × 2.1%) ÷ 2,100, using mid-2026 counts, so it is approximate.

slides.notes: The promotion (Feb–Aug 2025) gave 50% off for six months. 2,100 promo customers remain ($4.4M ARR at full price). If they churned like other SMB customers, SMB churn would be 2.1% instead of 3.1%: 1.0 of the 1.1-point rise.

slides.title: Price complaints rose only among promotion churners; core SMB looks no more price-sensitive than in 2025

paragraphs.text: IS IT AN ONBOARDING PROBLEM OR A PRICE PROBLEM?
Price complaints rose only among promotion churners; core SMB looks no more price-sensitive than in 2025
Churners citing price as main reason, % of survey respondents
The 34% is a mix, not a trend
It averages promo churners (52%) and other SMB churners (18%, flat vs. 19% in 2025).
Both sides are partly right
CFO: the core base is not leaving over price — yet.
CEO: price does drive exits where customers face a jump; promo customers saw +100% when the discount ended.
Customer Success: low activation explains only ~0.8 of the ~2.8-point gap; onboarding alone will not close it.

Source: Palisade Docs briefing pack, Nov 2026 (synthetic benchmark data) — Table 2 (exit-survey respondents citing “price / found a cheaper option”) and section 9. Decomposition is our estimate; see appendix.

slides.notes: Rough decomposition: if activated customers churn at rate a and low-activation customers at 3a, the 72%/28% mix of other SMB at 2.1% implies a ≈ 1.35%. With the promo cohort's 41%/59% mix that predicts ~2.9%, against ~4.9% implied. So activation explains about 0.8 of the 2.8-point gap; the rest coincides with the discount ending. Directional only.

slides.title: But Inkwell has made SMB price-sensitive at the point of sale: our contested win rate fell from 51% to 38%

paragraphs.text: COMPETITIVE EXPOSURE
But Inkwell has made SMB price-sensitive at the point of sale: our contested win rate fell from 51% to 38%
SMB win rate where Inkwell was considered
List price, $ per user per month
Implication
Raising SMB list price widens a $6 gap to $7.80 while we already lose 62% of contested deals. Mid-market and enterprise are not exposed: Inkwell has not appeared in deals above 200 seats.
Source: Palisade Docs briefing pack, Nov 2026 (synthetic benchmark data) — section 7.

slides.notes: A list-price rise also applies to new sign-ups. A 12% rise takes the SMB plan from $15 to $16.80 against Inkwell Starter at $9. Inkwell has not been seen in mid-market or enterprise deals over 200 seats; we do not know how much of mid-market is 51–200 seats.

slides.title: Pricing power sits in mid-market and enterprise, not in SMB

paragraphs.text: SEGMENT ASSESSMENT
Pricing power sits in mid-market and enterprise, not in SMB

data: 2023 +8%: churn 1.8% → 2.3% for six months, then 1.9% — before Inkwell
2024 +10% on new sign-ups: conversion 23.1% vs 23.6% (not significant)
Nothing cited; activation weak (41% in promo cohort)

paragraphs.text: Source: Palisade Docs briefing pack, Nov 2026 (synthetic benchmark data) — sections 5–9.

slides.notes: Colour shading: blue = supports a price rise, orange = argues against.

slides.title: The CFO’s $10.3M shrinks to ~$5–6M once renewal timing, contract caps and SMB churn are counted

paragraphs.text: TESTING THE CFO PLAN: +12% ON EVERY PLAN AT RENEWAL
The CFO’s $10.3M shrinks to ~$5–6M once renewal timing, contract caps and SMB churn are counted
Not in the $10.3M
Only 40% of enterprise and 85% of mid-market ARR renew in 2027.
SMB losses: ~320–640 customers, many likely to Inkwell.
Also unpriced
A list rise hits new SMB sign-ups, where we lose 62% of contested deals.
Mid-market +12% is above the only tested level (+10%).

Source: Palisade Docs briefing pack, Nov 2026 (synthetic benchmark data). SMB churn response scales the 2023 +8% pattern linearly to 12% (+3.6 pts of customers lost in year one × 1.5); stress case doubles it. Run-rate ARR at end-2027.

slides.notes: Arithmetic: headline 12% × $86.0M = $10.3M. Mid-market non-renewing 15% × $41.0M × 12% = $0.74M. Enterprise non-renewing 60% × $24.0M × 12% = $1.73M. Cap: $5.76M capped renewing ARR × 5 pts = $0.29M. Capturable $7.57M. SMB response: 5.4% of SMB ARR at new price ($23.5M) = $1.27M; stress 10.8% = $2.54M.

slides.title: Mid-market can absorb +10%; an SMB rise is a coin-flip that could net close to zero

paragraphs.text: RISK-REWARD BY SEGMENT
Mid-market can absorb +10%; an SMB rise is a coin-flip that could net close to zero
SMB +12%: net 2027 ARR gain, $M
Mid-market +10%
Run-rate uplift: 10% × $34.9M renewing ARR
Share of repriced ARR that would have to leave before the rise loses money — roughly doubling today’s ~9% annual logo churn
Why we expect far less:
2024 +10% test: no significant conversion effect
NRR 112%; integrations and audit trail keep customers
No Inkwell presence above 200 seats

Extra SMB customers lost: ~320 (2023 pattern) to ~640 (2×). Break-even is 10.7% of SMB ARR lost — the stress case (10.8%) sits on it. We cannot yet tell which case applies: that is uncertainty #1 in the pack.

Source: Palisade Docs briefing pack, Nov 2026 (synthetic benchmark data). Break-even share of repriced ARR lost = p ÷ (1 + p). SMB scenarios as on the previous slide. Mid-market annual churn ≈ 1 − (1 − 0.8%)^12 ≈ 9%.

slides.notes: For a price rise p, the rise loses money only if more than p/(1+p) of the repriced ARR leaves because of it: 9.1% at +10%, 10.7% at +12%.

slides.title: The segmented plan gives up to $2M of paper ARR to avoid an unmeasured bet on SMB

paragraphs.text: OPTIONS COMPARED
The segmented plan gives up to $2M of paper ARR to avoid an unmeasured bet on SMB

data:
A. CFO plan
+12% on every plan

B. Segmented (recommended)
MM +10%, Ent to terms, SMB hold + test
SMB churn response unknown; feeds Inkwell; MM priced above tested level
Relies on new-logo ARR or checkpoint upside to clear 15%
Misses growth goal; leaves MM/Ent value unused

paragraphs.text: Why B over A: A’s extra ARR is mostly the SMB rise, worth $0–1.3M net with downside, in the one segment where we lack evidence. B can recover most of it by July once the test shows whether the risk is real.

Source: Palisade Docs briefing pack, Nov 2026 (synthetic benchmark data). End-2027 ARR assumes each segment repeats its trailing-12-month NRR (+$8.0M on the base) plus price effects; new-logo ARR is excluded because the pack has no forecast.

slides.notes: Option B ranges include the checkpoint upside: mid-market H2 renewals stepped to 12% (+$0.35M) and SMB +8% on H2 renewals if the test passes (~+$0.5M net).

slides.title: The recommended plan gets ARR to ~$98.3M; closing the last $0.7M to the 15% goal needs new-logo ARR or the checkpoint upside

paragraphs.text: 2027 ARR BRIDGE, RECOMMENDED PLAN ($M)
The recommended plan gets ARR to ~$98.3M; closing the last $0.7M to the 15% goal needs new-logo ARR or the checkpoint upside
SMB pricing is not needed to reach the goal
Mid-market and enterprise expansion plus their price rises do most of the work.
SMB is the only segment shrinking on its own (−$1.3M at 94% NRR).
Checkpoint upside ≈ $0.85M
Mid-market H2 renewals at 12%: ~$0.35M.
SMB +8% on H2 renewals if test passes: ~$0.5M net.
Grey bar = the residual the pack cannot fill: it has no new-logo forecast.

Source: Palisade Docs briefing pack, Nov 2026 (synthetic benchmark data). Base movement = segment ARR × (trailing NRR − 1): SMB 94%, mid-market 112%, enterprise 118%. Assumes trailing NRR repeats; each 1 pt of overall NRR ≈ $0.9M.

slides.notes: This is a planning bridge, not a forecast. The pack contains no new-business pipeline, so new-logo ARR is shown as the residual needed to reach $98.9M.

slides.title: In SMB, fix activation and measure price sensitivity before repricing

paragraphs.text: THE SMB PLAN FOR H1 2027
In SMB, fix activation and measure price sensitivity before repricing
1  Hold list prices
2  Activation programme
3  Controlled renewal-price test
Keep SMB $15 and Business $29 through H1 2027.
Exclude the promo cohort from any 2027 rise — they cite price at 52% and just took a +100% step.
Revisit in July with test results.
Target customers sending <5 documents in month one (59% of the promo cohort).
Goal: bring promo-cohort churn (~4.9%) toward core SMB (2.1%).
Ceiling: SMB churn 3.1% → ~2.1%, a one-third cut — not the “halve in two quarters” claimed (1.55%, below any SMB level on record).
Randomly assign part of non-promo SMB renewals to +8% (the 2023 level we can benchmark); the rest stay at current price.
Measure 90-day churn and price-citing exits vs. control.
Also track Inkwell-contested win rate on new sign-ups.
Watch: core SMB churn (2.1%) and Inkwell-contested win rate (38%) do not worsen
Watch: share of new customers sending ≥5 documents in month one (72% today; 41% for promo)
Decides: whether SMB can take +8% on H2 renewals (July checkpoint)
Do not bank onboarding savings in the 2027 plan. Count them only once the activation rate of new cohorts moves.
Source: Palisade Docs briefing pack, Nov 2026 (synthetic benchmark data) — sections 6, 8, 10 and 11.

slides.notes: The Customer Success claim to halve SMB churn within two quarters is not supported by the pack. Halving 3.1% gives 1.55%, lower than any SMB level in the pack (2023 settled at 1.9%; core SMB is 2.1%). If the promo cohort behaved exactly like other SMB customers, SMB churn would be 2.1%, a one-third cut. Treat onboarding as upside, not plan.

slides.title: Six decisions for the December leadership meeting

paragraphs.text: DECISIONS REQUESTED
Six decisions for the December leadership meeting
Mid-market: +10% list price at renewal from January 2027
+$3.5M run-rate
Enterprise: raise at renewal to contract terms — 7% where capped, 10% otherwise
+$0.8M (ceiling)
SMB: hold list prices in H1 2027; exclude the promo cohort from any 2027 rise; approve the +8% renewal test
Avoids ~320–640 extra losses

Upside, not plan

slides.title: Appendix A — How the numbers were built

paragraphs.text: APPENDIX
Appendix A — How the numbers were built

data: Price caps spread evenly across renewing and non-renewing enterprise ARR
2023 +8%: +0.5 pt for 6 months, +0.1 pt after → +3.6 pts of customers in year one; ×1.5 for 12% = 5.4%; stress ×2 = 10.8%
Response scales linearly with price; stress multiple is illustrative
Mid-2026 counts stand for H1 averages
Other SMB: 72%×a + 28%×3a = 2.1% → a ≈ 1.35%; promo mix 41%/59% → ~2.9% predicted vs. ~4.9% implied
The “3×” ratio holds for all SMB; directional only
10% = the only tested level; enterprise figures are a ceiling
MM: 50% of renewing ARR in H2 × 2 pts = 0.35; SMB: 50% × 21.0 × 8% = 0.84 less 2023-style churn (3 pts × $11.3M = 0.34) = ~0.50
Renewals spread evenly over the year
Segment ARR × (trailing NRR − 1) = +$8.0M; plus price effects
Trailing NRR repeats in 2027; price rises add to it
Departures are a share of repriced ARR

Not in the pack — would sharpen the decision

ARR effects shown as end-2027 run-rate (the growth goal is an ARR goal); in-year revenue is lower because renewals fall through the year.
